summary: Specifies how packet information is exported from a PSAMP exporting process to a collecting process. It reuses the IPFIX protocol for the transport, since the two architectures match well. This document also covers how selected packet reports are carried using IPFIX mechanisms.

eli5.summary: After picking some packets to study, you have to send your notes to someone. This note says how to package and send those notes, borrowing the way another reporting system already works.

questions: how does psamp export packet data
what sampling methods does psamp support
subtitle: How a router reports the individual packets it sampled, by reusing the IPFIX export protocol.

tldr.problem: Network devices that pick out a subset of passing packets need a standard way to send reports about those packets, and the settings that produced them, to a collector.
tldr.mechanism: PSAMP export reuses the IPFIX protocol. Each selected packet becomes a Packet Report carried in a Data Record, and the sampling and filtering configuration travels in Options Template records called Report Interpretations.
tldr.outcome: A collector can decode the selected packets and also work out how they were chosen and how accurate they are. The only framework requirement not met is Export Packet compression.

today: RFC 5476 is a Proposed Standard published in March 2009. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why PSAMP Reuses IPFIX
sections.content:
The name PSAMP is a contraction of "Packet Sampling". Only a subset of the packets passing a network element is selected for reporting, using random selection, deterministic selection, or deterministic approximations to random selection (Hash-based Selection).

RFC 5476 specifies how information about those packets is exported from a PSAMP Exporting Process to a Collecting Process. Rather than invent a new protocol, it uses the IP Flow Information eXport (IPFIX) protocol from RFC 5101, because the two architectures match very well and the means IPFIX provides are sufficient. It is one of four PSAMP documents: the framework (RFC 5474), the selection techniques (RFC 5475), this protocol specification, and the information model (RFC 5477).
sections.eli5: Instead of building a brand new mail truck, the authors realized an existing one already fits, and just wrote down how to load it.

sections.title: Selection, Metering and Reporting
sections.content:
A Selection Process takes the Observed Packet Stream (all packets seen at the Observation Point) and selects a subset. A Selector decides, packet by packet, whether to keep it. A Composite Selector chains Selectors so the output of one feeds the next; a Selector that is not composite is a Primitive Selector with its own Selector ID, unique within the Observation Domain. The Selection Sequence is the combination of an Observation Point and the Selectors through which packets are selected.

Selectors are either Filtering (a deterministic choice based on packet content, such as matching a field or a hash range) or Sampling (anything else). The Metering Process, which always contains a Selection Process, produces a Report Stream of two kinds of information: Packet Reports about selected packets and Report Interpretation data such as the Selection Process configuration. The Exporting Process bundles them into Export Packets for the Collector.
sections.eli5: Think of a security guard who looks at every person walking by but only writes a report on some of them. The rules the guard follows are kept on a separate sheet.

sections.title: How PSAMP Differs From IPFIX
sections.content:
IPFIX measures traffic in two stages: packet processing, then Flow processing. PSAMP covers only stage 1, with packet classification replaced by Packet Report export. As a result, the PSAMP export can be seen as a special IPFIX Flow Record containing information about a single packet, and IPFIX does not distinguish such a record from one that aggregates several packets.

The protocol needed almost no changes. IPFIX already gained a flexible-length octet array type so that the first octets of a packet can be reported. Most Information Elements apply as they are, and the Sampling-related ones were intentionally left to the PSAMP information model in RFC 5477. A few, such as observedFlowTotalCount (always 1 for PSAMP), cannot be used meaningfully.

The RFC says the PSAMP protocol meets almost all of the requirements in the framework, including extensibility, parallel selection processes, accuracy, privacy and congestion avoidance. The one that is not met is Export Packet compression. Because PSAMP needs Data Sets, Template Sets and Options Template Sets, the entire IPFIX specification MUST be implemented.
sections.eli5: A flow record is like a summary of a whole conversation. A packet report is like a summary of a single sentence. The same form works for both, so no new form was needed.

sections.title: Packet Reports
sections.content:
For each selected packet in each Selection Sequence, a Packet Report MUST be created. Its format is given by an IPFIX Template Record, and the values go in a Data Record. A basic Packet Report MUST contain the selectionSequenceId and some contiguous bytes from the start of the packet (or from the start of its payload), carried in one of dataLinkFrameSection, mplsLabelStackSection, mplsPayloadPacketSection, ipPacketSection or ipPayloadPacketSection. If the Selection Sequence has a digest function, the hash value (digestHashValue) MUST be included too. The report SHOULD also carry a time element that matches the Metering Process accuracy, typically observationTimeMicroseconds.

Those byte fields may be fixed-length or variable-length. If a fixed-length field is longer than the bytes available, padding MUST NOT be used; the Exporting Process must send a new Template Record with the correct fixed length or a variable length.

An extended Packet Report MAY instead carry other Information Elements, such as source and destination addresses, output interface or a timestamp, and may omit the packet content to save bandwidth. The Exporting Process MUST also be able to limit the export rate to a configurable value.
sections.eli5: A packet report is a small card for each packet that was picked. It has the first bit of the packet copied onto it and a number saying which picking rules chose it.

sections.title: Report Interpretation
sections.content:
A collector needs more than the packet cards. Four kinds of Report Interpretation, each defined with an IPFIX Options Template Record, explain them.

  • Selection Sequence Report Interpretation: scoped by selectionSequenceId, it lists the Observation Point and the selectorId values, in the order they are used.
  • Selector Report Interpretation: scoped by selectorId, it carries the selectorAlgorithm and that algorithm's parameters.
  • Selection Sequence Statistics Report Interpretation: the number of packets observed and the number selected by each Primitive Selector. It MUST be exported periodically.
  • Accuracy Report Interpretation: SHOULD be sent so the collector can tell how accurate reported values such as timestamps are, using absoluteError or relativeError.

The statistics let a collector compute the Attained Selection Fraction. The RFC's example has 100 packets observed, 50 selected by a filter, then 6 by a one-out-of-ten sampler. The collector keeps the accuracy from the latest Accuracy Report Interpretation.
sections.eli5: If you only get the cards, you cannot tell how they were picked. So the sender also mails a rule sheet, a counting sheet that says how many were looked at, and a note about how precise the clock was.

sections.title: Selection Methods and Their Parameters
sections.content:
Each selection method gets its own selectorAlgorithm value and its own required parameters in the Selector Report Interpretation.

  • Systematic count-based sampling (value 1): samplingPacketInterval and samplingPacketSpace. A one-out-of-ten example uses an interval of 1 and a space of 9.
  • Systematic time-based sampling (value 2): samplingTimeInterval and samplingTimeSpace, in microseconds.
  • Random n-out-of-N sampling (value 3): samplingSize and samplingPopulation.
  • Uniform probabilistic sampling (value 4): samplingProbability.
  • Property match filtering (value 5): a packet is selected if fields equal predefined values. Several fields act as a logical AND; logical OR is not covered.
  • Hash-based filtering: BOB (6), IPSX (7) and CRC (8). Only BOB is recommended and SHOULD be used.

For hash-based selection, the hash input MUST include the IP identification field, flags, fragment offset, and source and destination addresses, plus a number of IP payload bytes. The minimum configuration ranges are 8 to 32 bytes for the number of payload bytes and 0 to 64 for the offset. Selected ranges MUST be non-overlapping. Encrypted fields that cannot be read MUST NOT cause a packet to be selected, but those packets still count in packetsObserved.

New methods MAY be added; each MUST be assigned a unique selectorAlgorithm value and its reporting parameters clearly specified.
sections.eli5: There are several ways to pick packets: every tenth one, one every so often by the clock, a random pick, or only the ones that look a certain way. Each way has a number so the receiver knows which was used.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content:
Because PSAMP security requirements are not stricter than IPFIX ones, the RFC points to RFC 5101 for the security considerations. It adds one rule of its own: a basic Packet Report exports only some contiguous bytes of a packet, and a PSAMP Device SHOULD NOT export the full payload of conversations, as that would amount to wiretapping (RFC 2804). The device MUST respect local privacy laws.

For IANA, numbers used by the protocol and information model follow RFC 5101. New selectorAlgorithm values are assigned on a First Come First Served basis, subject to Expert Review, with the experts initially drawn from the IPFIX and PSAMP Working Group chairs and document editors.
sections.eli5: The reporter should only copy the top of each packet, like reading an envelope, and never open the letters inside.
